To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the greater than 45S RNA fraction isolated from the immature and the mature pigeon erythroid cell contains about 40% of RNA sequences that are complementary to the unique and about 60% to the repetitive fraction of pigeon nuclear DNA.

(1) in bone marrow, the repetitive and the unique DNA sequences transcribe greater than 45S RNA at a ratio of 3 : 2, (2) in the immature (reticulocytes) and the mature (erythrocytes) erythroid cells, the ratio is approximately 1 : 3, and (3) in the erythroid cells the greater than 45 RNA hybridised with the unique DNA is of a lower molecular weight than the one
the fraction of greater than 40 S RNA hybridising with repetitive DNA sequences in bone marrow is 20%, in reticulocytes 13% and in erythrocytes only 6%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcription of repetitive DNA sequences in pigeon erythrocytes of different degrees of specialization.
the study of the transcription of the repetitive and unique nucleotide sequences of pigeon DNA in erythroid cells at different stages of maturation.
a comparison of transcription of the repetitive and unique DNA sequences in pigeon erythroblasts with different degrees of maturity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the erythroid cells the proportion of greater than 46 S RNA hybridised with repetitive sequences increases as the cells mature and become more specialized.
the greater than 45 s HnRNAs from immature and mature erythrocytes are not identical in terms of their content of repetitive and unique sequences.
the greater the degree of erythroid cell specialization the lower is the fraction of greater than 40S RNA which is hybridisable with the repetitive sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in all three types of pigeon erythroid cell the greater than 45 s RNA fraction is composed of a considerable number of molecules hybridizing with the repetitive DNA sequences and that the number of such molecules decreases with the degree of specialization of the cells.
the degree of specialization of erythroid cells is reflected in the pattern of transcription of DNA.

the greater than 45S RNAs from the immature erythroid cells (bone marrow) are hybridised with both the repetitive and unique sequences of the genome, whereas in the mature erythroid cell (reticulocytes and erythrocytes) the hybridisation with the repetitive fraction is considerably reduced and the hybridisation with unique fraction remains unchanged.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the greater than 45S RNA of immature erythroid cells contains a higher proportion of repetitive DNA sequences than the greater than 40S RNA of mature erythroid and non-erythroid cells.

the greater than 45S RNA from bone marrow and immature and mature erythrocyte populations of pigeon are heterogeneous with respect to their ability to hybridise with the repetitive and unique DNA sequences.
the transcription of repetitive DNA sequences in immature erythroid cells is not restricted to the early phases of erythropoiesis.
